comments.text: I find Bhutan fascinating because it challenges the idea that money is the key to a good life. But I wonder, can happiness really come first when people still have bills to pay? What do you think?

comments.author: @TravelHorizon-4K
comments.text: The $100-per-night Sustainable Development Fee [01:19] keeps crowds low and funds healthcare and education [39:10], yet on the flip side it turns visiting Bhutan into a privilege for higher-income travelers [55:02]. What do you think—is high pricing to protect the country or greater access for average travelers fairer and more sustainable?

comments.author: @travelintolifeus
comments.text: Bhutan makes you question what we really mean when we talk about a good life. Between the peaceful mountain villages, strong family traditions, and respect for nature, there’s something deeply inspiring about a country that measures progress differently. I wish more places valued these things.
